summary_html: Agency **files a court petition** to open a **dependency** (or similar) case. Federal funding frameworks (IV-E/ASFA) link court oversight, reasonable-efforts findings, and permanency timelines to downstream actions.
authority_html:
- **ASFA / SSA Title IV-E** — court findings; timelines; permanency planning  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of court/agency performance measures

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: In re Interest of Borius H.
key_cases.holding: The court reaffirmed that every motion for an ex parte temporary detention order must be supported by an affidavit of a person with knowledge, held that the State must prove the requirements of Neb. Rev. Stat. § 43-254 by a preponderance of the evidence at the detention hearing, and ordered dismissal because the State adduced no evidence at that hearing.
key_cases.relevance: The decision governs the county attorney's motion for temporary custody filed alongside the juvenile petition.
key_cases.quote: we once again state that all motions for ex parte temporary detention orders must be accompanied by an affidavit of one who has knowledge of relevant facts warranting temporary detention

key_cases.case_name: In re Interest of Mainor T.
key_cases.holding: The court held that plain error permeated the proceedings because the mother had a statutory right to counsel under § 43-279.01 but was unrepresented and had not waived counsel at adjudication, and that she was denied due process; the abandonment finding and the termination of her parental rights were reversed.
key_cases.relevance: The due process defects the court identifies begin at the filing and adjudication stage, not at termination.
key_cases.quote: Our de novo review of the record demonstrates that during these proceedings, Mercedes was denied due process.

key_cases.case_name: In re Interest of Jeremy U.
key_cases.holding: The court held that 'lacks proper parental care' in § 43-247(3)(a) refers to the type and nature of the care a child is receiving rather than to who provides it, so the two children living safely with grandparents could not be adjudicated on that ground, while the child living with the mother should have been adjudicated.
key_cases.relevance: The court tells the State it may petition again only if it acquires evidence that the children actually lack proper care, constraining petition practice.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that "parental" as used in the phrase "lacks proper parental care" describes the type and nature of care rather than the relationship of the person providing it.

key_cases.case_name: In re Interest of Xandria P.
key_cases.holding: The court held that the child's recorded child-advocacy-center forensic interview was properly admitted under the rule 803(3) medical diagnosis or treatment exception and that the State proved the allegations of the § 43-247(3)(a) petition by a preponderance of the evidence.
key_cases.relevance: It states the burden the State carries on the petition it files to open a dependency case.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that the State sustained the adjudication petition by a preponderance of the evidence

key_cases.holding: The court held that a short-term ex parte temporary detention order is not final while an order entered after a detention hearing that continues to keep custody from the parent pending adjudication is appealable, and that on this record due process did not require the mother's counsel to be present at the temporary detention hearing because the juvenile court refused to take notice of that testimony at adjudication and she was represented at every later stage.
key_cases.relevance: The court refused to review the sufficiency of the juvenile petition because the petition was never made part of the record, an evidentiary discipline that governs any challenge to the petition opening a dependency case.
key_cases.quote: considering the procedures used in this case, due process did not require the presence of the mother's counsel at the temporary detention hearing

key_cases.case_name: In re Interest of Brian B. et al.
key_cases.holding: The court held that the juvenile court properly exercised its discretion in allowing the child to testify in chambers with counsel present, that the procedures used adequately safeguarded the father's due process rights, and that the allegations of the petition were proved by a preponderance of the evidence, affirming the adjudication of all three children under § 43-247(3)(a).
key_cases.relevance: It is the authority In re Interest of Xandria P. relies on for the framework the brief uses at this node: the adjudication phase exists to protect the child, and the parents' rights are determined at disposition, not at adjudication.
key_cases.quote: The purpose of the adjudication phase of a juvenile proceeding is to protect the interests of the child.
